title: Are Latent Reasoning Models Easily Interpretable?
summary: This research investigates the interpretability of latent reasoning models (Coconut and CODI). It finds that for logical tasks, these models rely on training data rather than hidden reasoning steps, as stopping early doesn't change outputs. However, for math problems, hidden states often encode correct intermediate steps, decodable up to 93% of the time, enabling prediction of answer correctness.
